value.positive_en: What is angioplasty, also called PCI, used to do in coronary arteries narrowed or blocked by plaque?
value.positive_zh: 血管成形术（也叫PCI）用于对被斑块变窄或堵塞的冠状动脉做什么？
value.evidence: Angioplasty is a procedure to improve blood flow in coronary arteries that have become narrow or blocked. Your coronary arteries supply oxygen-rich blood to your heart. If you have coronary artery disease , a sticky material called plaque builds up in your coronary arteries. Plaque is made of cholesterol , calcium, and other substances in your blood. Over time, it can narrow your arteries or fully block them. When this happens, some parts of your heart don't get enough blood. Angioplasty widens the blocked part of your artery so more blood can get through. It is also called percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
value.expected_answer: Angioplasty, or PCI, widens the blocked part of a coronary artery to improve blood flow so more blood can get through.
value.missing_en: What exact percentage of patients have the artery narrow again after angioplasty for coronary artery disease?
value.missing_reason: The summary does not state a precise restenosis percentage; it only says serious problems do not happen very often and may include narrowing of the artery again.
